items.name: result-card
items.title: ResultCard
items.description: One test result, showing the number, what it is compared against, and what it means.

items.name: range-bar
items.title: RangeBar
items.description: A bar showing where one reading sits against the range it is compared with.

items.name: score-dial
items.title: ScoreDial
items.description: A single composite number drawn as a ring, with the words that say what it counts.

items.name: trend-sparkline
items.title: TrendSparkline
items.description: A small chart of one reading over time, with an honest caption saying what changed.

items.name: metric-tile
items.title: MetricTile
items.description: A compact tile showing one reading, its unit and when it was taken.

items.name: status-pill
items.title: StatusPill
items.description: A short label saying what a reading means and what, if anything, to do about it.

items.name: alert-banner
items.title: AlertBanner
items.description: A prominent message about something that needs the reader's attention now.

items.name: care-card
items.title: CareCard
items.description: A card saying what to do next, and how urgently.

items.name: term
items.title: Term
items.description: A clinical word shown in plain English, with the original available on demand.

items.name: consent-sheet
items.title: ConsentSheet
items.description: A sheet that asks permission for one specific thing, and records the answer.

items.name: disclaimer-note
items.title: DisclaimerNote
items.description: The standing note about what this information is and is not.

items.name: log-sheet
items.title: LogSheet
items.description: A form for writing down what happened today, in as few taps as possible.

items.name: reading-input
items.title: ReadingInput
items.description: An input for typing in a measurement, with the unit shown and switchable beside the number.

items.name: value
items.title: Value
items.description: One number and its unit, formatted the same way everywhere in the product.

items.name: relative-time
items.title: RelativeTime
items.description: When a reading was taken, said the way a person would say it.

items.name: surface
items.title: Surface
items.description: The base panel every other surface is built from, at one of six material rungs.

items.name: card
items.title: Card
items.description: A bounded block of related content.

items.name: sheet
items.title: Sheet
items.description: A panel that slides over the screen and can be dismissed by dragging.

items.name: dialog
items.title: Dialog
items.description: A window that interrupts, for the one decision that cannot wait.

items.name: callout
items.title: Callout
items.description: A short piece of set-apart information — a note, a tip, a caveat — that helps you understand what you are reading without claiming anything about your health.

items.name: empty-state
items.title: EmptyState
items.description: What a screen shows when there is nothing to show, and what to do about it.

items.name: skeleton
items.title: Skeleton
items.description: The shape of content that has not arrived yet.

items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.description: The control that makes something happen.

items.name: field
items.title: Field
items.description: A labelled input with its help text, its error, and the wiring that connects them.

items.name: questionnaire
items.title: Questionnaire
items.description: A multi-question form for a validated instrument such as a symptom score.
items.why: Validated instruments are licensed, scored and interpreted by their publishers, and a component that renders one invites a product to alter its wording or its scoring. That is a clinical-safety problem no amount of API design fixes.

items.name: symptom-picker
items.title: SymptomPicker
items.description: A picker for choosing symptoms from a controlled list.
items.why: A symptom picker is one step from a symptom checker, and a symptom checker is a regulated device in most of the markets this system targets. The controlled vocabulary is also product-specific and cannot be shipped in a design system.

items.name: dose-tracker
items.title: DoseTracker
items.description: A record of medicine doses taken and missed.
items.why: Dose data drives dosing decisions. A component that displays a missed dose is one product decision away from implying what to do about it, which is prescribing.

items.name: body-map
items.title: BodyMap
items.description: A diagram of a body for pointing at where something hurts.
items.why: A body diagram must represent a range of bodies, ages, skin tones and disabilities, or it tells some readers they are not the intended user. Doing that properly is an illustration commission, not a component.

items.name: goal-ring
items.title: GoalRing
items.description: Progress towards a daily goal, drawn as a closing ring.
items.why: Goal rings are strongly associated with one platform's fitness product, and the pattern rewards streaks — which is the wrong incentive for a reader managing a condition rather than training for one.

items.name: timeline-entry
items.title: TimelineEntry
items.description: One dated event in a vertical history.
items.why: A timeline is a layout, and every product's timeline holds different things. Shipping one would ship a data model with it.

items.name: scale-input
items.title: ScaleInput
items.description: A one-to-ten scale for rating something like pain or mood.
items.why: The anchors and the number of points on a rating scale are what make it comparable over time, and they belong to whichever instrument the product is using.

items.name: source-citation
items.title: SourceCitation
items.description: Where a piece of health information came from, and when it was last checked.
items.why: Strongly wanted and likely to be promoted. Held back only because provenance is currently doctrine rather than a component, and shipping the box before the rules would encourage products to cite whatever is to hand.

items.name: range-legend
items.title: RangeLegend
items.description: The key explaining what the bands on a range mean.
items.why: A legend that can be separated from its chart is a legend that will be. The bands are documented inside RangeBar instead.

items.name: toast
items.title: Toast
items.description: A brief message that appears and disappears on its own.
items.why: A message that removes itself is the wrong shape for anything about someone's health: the reader who most needs it is the one most likely to miss it. Kept on the roster because products use toasts for save confirmations, which is legitimate.

items.name: tooltip
items.title: Tooltip
items.description: A short label that appears on hover or focus.
items.why: There is no hover on a phone, and this is a phone-first system. Anything important enough for a tooltip is important enough to be on the screen.

items.name: popover
items.title: Popover
items.description: A small panel anchored to the control that opened it.
items.why: Base UI's popover is complete and unopinionated, and opsinjs has nothing to add to it beyond tokens.

items.name: tabs
items.title: Tabs
items.description: Switching between views that occupy the same space.
items.why: Delegated to Base UI unchanged. Documented in the handbook rather than re-wrapped.

items.name: accordion
items.title: Accordion
items.description: Sections that expand one at a time.
items.why: Delegated to Base UI unchanged. Note that hiding a safety message inside a collapsed section is a defect regardless of the component used.

items.name: select
items.title: Select
items.description: Choosing one option from a list.
items.why: Delegated to Base UI. opsinjs adds guidance — for short lists a radio group is easier for the reader — rather than a component.

items.name: combobox
items.title: Combobox
items.description: A text input that filters a list as you type.
items.why: Delegated to Base UI. The hard part in a health product is the vocabulary being searched, not the widget.

items.name: switch
items.title: Switch
items.description: An on-or-off control that takes effect immediately.
items.why: Delegated to Base UI. A switch must never be used for consent — consent is a decision with a record, not a setting.

items.name: checkbox
items.title: Checkbox
items.description: A box for choosing any number of options, including none.
items.why: Delegated to Base UI.

items.name: radio-group
items.title: RadioGroup
items.description: A set of options where exactly one can be chosen.
items.why: Delegated to Base UI. Preferred over Select for anything under about seven options.

items.name: slider
items.title: Slider
items.description: Choosing a value by dragging along a track.
items.why: Delegated to Base UI, and discouraged for entering a measurement: a slider cannot express precision, and a reading typed in is a reading the person meant.

items.name: number-field
items.title: NumberField
items.description: An input for a number, with steppers.
items.why: Delegated to Base UI. ReadingInput is the health-aware wrapper, and it is on the shipped roster.

items.name: textarea
items.title: Textarea
items.description: A multi-line text input.
items.why: A native element that needs tokens, not a component.

items.name: progress
items.title: Progress
items.description: How far through something the reader is.
items.why: Delegated to Base UI. Never use it to show a health value: a progress bar implies a target, and most readings do not have one.

items.name: spinner
items.title: Spinner
items.description: An indeterminate loading indicator.
items.why: Skeletons are preferred throughout: a skeleton says what is arriving, and a spinner says only that something is.

items.name: badge
items.title: Badge
items.description: A small label attached to something else.
items.why: Kept off the shipped roster deliberately: a generic badge next to a StatusPill is exactly how the two colour axes get mixed. If you need a badge to carry a health meaning, you need a StatusPill.

items.name: divider
items.title: Divider
items.description: A line separating two groups of content.
items.why: A border and a spacing token. Documented in Foundations rather than shipped.

items.name: scroll-area
items.title: ScrollArea
items.description: A scrolling region with styled scrollbars.
items.why: Delegated to Base UI. Custom scrollbars are also a frequent cause of unreachable content at 200% text.

items.name: tab-bar
items.title: TabBar
items.description: The persistent bar of top-level destinations at the bottom of the screen.
items.why: Application navigation is a product decision, not a design-system one. The material rung, the safe-area handling and the touch-target floor it needs are all documented.

items.name: segmented-control
items.title: SegmentedControl
items.description: A small row of mutually exclusive options.
items.why: Likely to be promoted — it is the right control for switching a chart between day, week and month. Held back until TrendSparkline exists to use it.

items.name: stepper
items.title: Stepper
items.description: Progress through a sequence of steps.
items.why: The pattern that matters is one question per page, and that is documented in Patterns. A stepper component tends to encourage the opposite.

items.name: menu
items.title: Menu
items.description: A list of actions opened from a button.
items.why: Delegated to Base UI. Hiding a destructive or a safety-relevant action in an overflow menu is a defect whatever renders it.

items.name: icon-button
items.title: IconButton
items.description: A button whose only visible content is an icon.
items.why: A variant of Button rather than a component, and one that needs a visible label far more often than products assume.

items.name: link
items.title: Link
items.description: Navigation to somewhere else.
items.why: An element with tokens and a routing decision the product owns. What opsinjs adds is guidance about link text, and that belongs in Content and language.

items.name: avatar
items.title: Avatar
items.description: A picture or initials standing for a person.
items.why: Straightforward to build and full of representation decisions — default imagery, initials for names that do not have them, and what a clinician's avatar implies about who wrote a message.

items.name: table
items.title: Table
items.description: Rows and columns of data.
items.why: Every chart in this system ships a table twin, so a table is a requirement rather than an option — but a responsive, accessible table is a project of its own and would be the largest component here by an order of magnitude.

items.name: visually-hidden
items.title: VisuallyHidden
items.description: Content that screen readers announce and eyes do not see.
items.why: Four lines of CSS that every component here uses internally, shipped as a utility class rather than as a component so that it works outside React too.
